leftEvidence.title: David orders gentleness and Absalom dies

points.label: Action and response
points.left: David organizes the army, is persuaded to remain, publicly commands gentleness for Absalom, while the forest battle ends with Joab and armor bearers killing the suspended son.
points.right: Ahimaaz and the Cushite compete to report, David repeatedly asks about the young man, hears Absalom is dead, and withdraws crying that he wished he had died instead.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places the king’s public command and the commander’s action diverge inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places public deliverance arrives as private devastation inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 18:1–18 and 2 Samuel 18:19–33 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Exile, Return, and Rebellion” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: News of victory becomes a father’s grief

payload.tension: 2 Samuel 18:1–18 foregrounds the king’s public command and the commander’s action diverge; 2 Samuel 18:19–33 foregrounds public deliverance arrives as private devastation. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
